hypothesis: Question: on development patients never seen in training, does any regularized voice-based or demographics-only model transfer better than the constant median, and is the reference models' loss to the median explained by row-level fitting of patient-specific offsets? Prior evidence (development, patient-held-out, single 7-patient split): median 8.379 loss / 7.427 patient-MAE, standardized Ridge(alpha 10) 8.523 / 7.490, HGB(250 it.) 10.465 / 8.909. Both fitted references lose to the median, which is consistent with learning non-transferable patient offsets, but one split cannot separate 'no transferable voice signal' from 'under-regularized fits'. Round-1 attempt idea-8e7efc pursued this question but failed operationally (ValueError: private/reflection and I/O attributes unsupported) before producing any measurement; that failure is not a negative result, so the scientific question is unchanged. This rewrite avoids all dunder/underscore attribute access, json/I-O calls and classes. Inside fit_predict, using train data only, it scores 13 candidates (median, mean, age+sex linear, age+sex+test_time linear, standardized Ridge alpha 10/100/1000 with and without log1p of jitter/shimmer/NHR, voice-only log Ridge, shallow strongly regularized HGB on all and on voice-only columns) by 7-fold GroupKFold over the 28 train patients (RMSE and equal-patient MAE) plus a shuffled 5-fold row-level KFold for contrast; the lowest group-CV RMSE candidate is refitted on all train and predicts development. Contrasting expected outcomes: (A) group-CV picks the median or a demographics-only linear model and every voice model shows a large row-minus-group CV gap, supporting 'voice adds little beyond patient identity on 28 patients'; (B) a heavily regularized or log-transformed voice model wins group-CV and improves development loss below 8.379, supporting 'references were under-regularized'; (C) group-CV winner still loses on development, indicating 28-patient selection is itself noisy. Findings report the full candidate table, between-patient variance fraction of train y, the chosen model, and any fallback use. No transductive use of unlabeled inputs; all scaling statistics come from train folds. Exploratory joint changes; no single-factor attribution claimed.
